programmes.name: Foundation Strength
programmes.summary: Full-body basics: push, pull, legs and core three times a week. Builds the base for every later programme.
programmes.progression: Weeks 1–2: stay at the low end of each range. Week 3: add a rep per set. Week 4: when you reach the top of every range, move to a harder variation (lower incline, feet-elevated rows).

programmes.name: First Pull-up
programmes.summary: Six weeks of hangs, scapular work, negatives and rows aimed at getting your first strict pull-up.
programmes.progression: Weeks 1–2: learn the movements. Weeks 3–4: lengthen the negatives to 5 s and thin the band. Weeks 5–6: test a strict pull-up at the start of Day A each week.

programmes.name: Handstand Foundations
programmes.summary: Short, frequent sessions to build wrist strength, shoulder stacking and a solid wall handstand.
programmes.progression: Week 1: hold the wall handstand for 15 s. Add 5 s each week as long as your ribs stay tucked and arms stay straight. Stop a set when form breaks.

programmes.name: 2-Week Mobility Reset
programmes.summary: Fifteen easy minutes a day to open shoulders, wrists, hips and hamstrings.
programmes.progression: Alternate upper and lower flows across the five days. Keep every stretch comfortable; move gently in and out and never bounce.

programmes.name: Circuit Kickstart
programmes.summary: Three weeks of simple circuits to build work capacity and get into a routine.

exercises.name: Bodyweight squats
exercises.note: Circuit: 4 rounds, 60–90 s rest between rounds

programmes.progression: Week 1: 3 rounds per circuit. Week 2: 4 rounds. Week 3: keep 4 rounds and shorten rest by 15 s.

programmes.name: Push / Pull / Legs Hypertrophy
programmes.summary: A classic push, pull and legs split using bodyweight variations to build muscle.
programmes.progression: Add a rep to each set every week. In week 4 reduce sets by one (easy week). In week 6 use slower lowering (3 s) or a harder variation once you reach the top of each range.

programmes.name: Front Lever Path
programmes.summary: Progress from tuck to advanced tuck front lever with supporting pulling and core work.
programmes.progression: Move to the advanced tuck when you hold a tuck for 5 sets of 15 s with flat back and straight arms. Keep the best hold quality, not the longest time.

programmes.name: Muscle-up Prep
programmes.summary: Build the pulling height, explosive power and transition needed for a bar muscle-up.
programmes.progression: Weeks 1–2: pull-up height and strength. Weeks 3–4: add the transition drills. Week 5: test a low-bar muscle-up attempt on Day B.

programmes.name: Superset Strength Blocks
programmes.summary: Pair opposing movements back to back to fit more work into each session.

exercises.name: A1 Pull-ups
exercises.note: Superset A1/A2, rest 90 s after each pair

programmes.progression: Week 1: use the low end of each range. Add a rep per set each week. Keep rest strict at 90 s after each pair.

programmes.name: Mobility for Skills
programmes.summary: Shoulder, wrist and hip mobility work that supports handstands, levers and planche.
programmes.progression: Do each session after a short warm-up. Week 2: add 10 s to each hold. Week 3: add a third round of the wrists and shoulders.

programmes.name: Planche Progression
programmes.summary: Structured tuck to advanced tuck planche development with straight-arm conditioning.
programmes.progression: Straight-arm work stresses wrists and elbows. Add time gradually and keep at least one rest day between sessions. Move up a progression once you hold 5 sets of 10 s cleanly.

programmes.name: Handstand Push-up Path
programmes.summary: Wall handstand push-up negatives, presses and supporting pushing volume.
programmes.progression: Weeks 1–2: negatives and partial range. Weeks 3–4: reduce the assistance. Week 5: test full-range repetitions on Day C.

programmes.name: Weighted Calisthenics Strength
programmes.summary: Low-rep weighted pulling, pushing and single-leg work for maximum strength.
programmes.progression: When you hit the top of the rep range on every set, add 1–2.5 kg next session. Rest 2–3 min between heavy sets. Deload in week 4 by halving the sets.

programmes.name: One-Arm Pull-up Prep
programmes.summary: Advanced pulling strength and one-arm specific work. Needs a strong weighted pull-up base.
programmes.progression: Elbow and shoulder tendons adapt slowly. Start with fewer sets in weeks 1–2, and stop any session where elbow pain appears.

programmes.name: Skills and Strength Peak
programmes.summary: High-level lever, planche and handstand work alongside weighted strength.

exercises.name: Advanced tuck to straddle front lever

programmes.progression: Stagger skills across the week and keep 24–48 h between straight-arm sessions. Trade volume for quality; stop sets when holds begin to degrade.

programmes.name: 1-Week Deload
programmes.summary: An easy week: half the usual volume plus mobility, to recover between harder blocks.
programmes.progression: Stop every set well before failure. Sleep and eat well, then restart your regular programme the following week.

workouts.name: Full-Body Basics
workouts.summary: A balanced starter session covering every major movement pattern.

workouts.name: 10-Minute Morning Mobility
workouts.summary: A quick wake-up flow for shoulders, spine and hips.

workouts.name: Beginner Circuit
workouts.summary: Four exercises, four rounds, steady pace.

workouts.name: Core Starter
workouts.summary: Basic trunk strength with low-risk positions.

workouts.name: Wall Handstand Practice
workouts.summary: Practice stacking against the wall with short, high-quality holds.

workouts.name: Push Day
workouts.summary: Dips, pike push-ups and triceps work.

workouts.name: Pull Day
workouts.summary: Vertical and horizontal pulling with core.

workouts.name: Push / Pull Superset
workouts.summary: Pair each pull with a push to keep the session efficient.

workouts.name: Static Hold Circuit
workouts.summary: Rotate through skill holds with short rests.
workouts.rest: Rest 45 s between holds, 90 s between rounds

workouts.name: Shoulder and Wrist Prep
workouts.summary: Prepare the joints before pushing or straight-arm skill work.

workouts.name: Planche Skill Session
workouts.summary: Planche progression practice with warm-up and finishing work.

workouts.name: Front Lever Session
workouts.summary: Front lever holds, rows and scapular control.

workouts.name: Hips and Hamstrings Mobility
workouts.summary: Longer holds to improve straddle, pancake and pike positions.

workouts.name: Max Strength: Weighted Pull and Dips
workouts.summary: Heavy, low-rep work with long rests.

workouts.name: Skill Complex Circuit
workouts.summary: Move through advanced holds and presses in a cycle.
workouts.rest: Rest 60 s between stations, 2 min between rounds

workouts.name: One-Arm Pull-up Session
workouts.summary: Specific one-arm pulling work; warm up thoroughly.
